text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.44% today, extending a strong recovery from a 6.76% two-week dip. The recovery momentum reflects a sharp rebound in crude and refined product prices — US oil is trading at $89.62/barrel while refineries are running at 95.2% capacity utilization, near peak efficiency. Refiners like Marathon profit when they can process crude into gasoline and diesel at high margins, and with heating oil prices up 59% year-over-year heading into winter, demand for refined fuels remains elevated.

However, the recent news reveals a crosswind: Russian crude production has rebounded strongly after a Trump administration diesel deal, pushing global oil supplies back into surplus territory according to the IEA. While this kept oil prices from rising further, it also means refiners face more plentiful input costs going forward, which could compress the margins that have been driving the stock's recent recovery.
